edges.description: Tick inoculation delivers R. japonica to intracellular host-cell niches.
Local dermal infection at the bite site can necrose into an eschar.
Intracellular R. japonica remains dependent on bacterial ribosomal protein synthesis.
Disseminated endothelial infection produces vasculitic tissue injury.
Cutaneous microvascular inflammation contributes to the exanthem.
Vasculitic vascular injury permits purpuric hemorrhage into skin.
Disseminated endothelial inflammation amplifies systemic cytokine release.
Widespread small-vessel injury can extend into renal, pulmonary, and hepatic organ injury.
Cytokine-amplified severe disease predisposes to DIC.
Fulminant inflammatory injury can progress to renal and pulmonary failure.
Systemic consumptive coagulation manifests as DIC.
Consumptive coagulation lowers the circulating platelet count.
Severe DIC can produce purpura fulminans with ischemic skin injury.
Severe systemic JSF commonly injures the liver.
Fulminant systemic JSF can include neurological involvement.
